summary: Red Mountain lookout in Lewis and Clark County: a D-6 cabin dated 1929 but disputed, removed after the mid-1950s. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin, set on the ground
facts.status_note: Cabin removed after the mid-1950s per firelookout.com. No source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: firelookout.com dates the D-6 cupola cabin to 1929. A 1925 item and a 1923 photo caption suggest the site was in use earlier. The sources disagree.
Clarence Graham was a lookout on Red Mountain in 1936, per a 1938 newspaper item quoted on the Montana Lookouts page.
A July 1939 item said the Red Mountain station would be replaced by one on Stonewall Mountain.
Abandoned in the 1940s, per firelookout.com. 1940 is a placeholder year because the source gives only the decade.
Still standing in the mid-1950s and removed since. 1955 is a placeholder year; the source gives no removal date.

notes_for_editor: Distance: firelookout.com gives about 11 miles north of Lincoln; the 1956 survey datasheet, quoted on the weebly page, gives about 12 miles north-northwest. The story attributes each figure. Identity risk: the Forest Fire Lookout Association list has a second Red Mountain in Lewis & Clark County at 47.16295, -112.44249 (Camp Abandoned; firelookout.com/mt/redmtn399.html, 7,161 ft, 1930s camp, 18 miles NE of Lincoln). The repo already has us-mt-red-mountain-2.json for it. The 1925 item's Lander's Fork location cannot be matched to either site from the text alone; check a map before publishing. Dates disagree: firelookout.com gives 1929; the 1925 item says construction was about to begin and a lookout had been kept for two years; a 1923 photo caption calls it a proposed lookout. Elevation is 9,411 ft on firelookout.com and 9,390 ft in the 1925 item. The only source on the summit today is the 1956 survey description, quoted on the weebly page; the NGS datasheet itself was not fetched. Staffing is known only for 1936, and there are no fire records.
